title: Rex Fleet #1 — The Green Corridor
summary: Briefly establish that the Shattering destroyed reliable fast routes, that generations endured very slow interstellar travel, and that newly reblazed reciprocal-field passages again make distant communities reachable. Lead immediately into a Verge-owned grain freighter carrying ordinary migrants.
settingText: EDITORIAL OPENING — CIVILIAN GRAIN ROUTE AND SHATTERED FRONTIER
panelPlan: Single editorial splash with measured green beacon references defining a newly reblazed high-speed reciprocal-field corridor beyond a recognizable Verge agricultural departure world. Distinguish the stabilized field-transit volume from slower physical docking and wreck-field approaches.

Foreground Verge grain freighter visibly carries owned agricultural freight and civilian relocation passengers; the Fleet's escort is separate and does not appear to control or possess the grain. Small distant Shard traffic may be present without implying a current attack.

Text occupies a calm dark negative-space field at the upper left or a restrained block integrated into an unobstructed part of the scene. Do not invent chart labels, inscriptions, names or faux-interface writing.
The last line should lead directly into the opening Luminara dock scene. This is narration for the reader, not a person speaking in the scene.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Shattering broke the fast routes connecting settled worlds.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Generations learned to survive journeys measured in months and years.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now a newly reblazed crossing makes Auric reachable again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A Verge freighter is preparing to take it.

directionInline.text: This is the sole editorial context needed before Issue 1. Explain the practical stakes of separation and grain movement without forecasting later outcomes, issuing a moral verdict or teaching the full technical history of the Shattering.
Treat reciprocal-field transit as physical science. Use precise ship geometry, restrained navigational green and lived-in infrastructure. Only scripted captions and display lettering are readable.

title: From the Editor — The Frontier Ahead
summary: Issue 1 end matter introduces the series' human and political promises, traces how the Shattering and reopened corridors reshape the frontier, discloses the playful use of AI, and previews Issue 2 and two companion stories.
settingText: STAR SPLITTER VISIONS EDITORIAL PAGE — THE REX FLEET FRONTIER
panelPlan: Create a genuine end-matter editorial page, not a story splash. At the top, use the established Star Splitter Visions / REX FLEET masthead treatment matching the approved Issue 2 masthead, with the Issue 1 identifier.

Below it, use a dramatic, series-promotional hero image distinct from the Issue 2 cover composition. Place Naomi Sol, Commodore Ella Venn, and Tessa Banks as the human focal figures against a vivid frontier where Verge, Fleet, and Shard interests meet. The image should promise a multi-sided human space opera, not depict one specific Issue 2 scene.

Set the editor's letter beneath the hero in a magazine-quality two-column grid on cool white and pale blue-gray, using dark navy serif body text, clear sans-serif headings, generous line spacing, and a restrained amount of gold, green, and red accent. Keep all copy exactly as scripted and legible.

Use the lower right of the letter area for a compact three-step visual timeline: the Shattering breaks fast routes; generations grow up separated; the corridors reopen and bring distant communities back into contact. Treat it as a historical sequence, not a precise geographic map or invented interface.

Place the candid Star Splitter Visions AI note in a distinct, quiet inset. In the lower rail, include a small inset reproducing the supplied approved Issue 2 cover artwork exactly under SEE NEXT; do not redesign or substitute its cover. Include the Issue 2 label and the supplied tagline.

Balance the opposite lower column with the two supplied COMING SOON teasers: Rex Fleet Academy: Reach and Resolve, and Shattering of the Corridors. The page should feel finished and composed at the 5:8 page ratio, with no repeated character-head strip, no yellow cast, and no unused blank block.

Only scripted masthead, headings, editorial copy, teaser copy, and lettering already present in the supplied Issue 2 cover may be readable. Do not invent credits, signage, chart labels, faux-interface text, or additional slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Three powers share one frontier. When the Green Corridor opens, Naomi Sol guides a freighter of families toward a future they thought out of reach. A Shard cutter shadows them. Commodore Ella Venn sends the Fleet to protect the passage—an act of rescue to some, a claim of power to others.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Naomi wants her passengers to arrive with their choices intact. Ella must decide where protection ends and command begins. At Black Drift, Abby, Billie, and Tessa prepare another raid. The cargo could feed their families; Fleet expansion is turning old allies against each other.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Rex Fleet is about the people caught between survival, security, and home.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: As routes reopen, neighbors become strangers, rivals become uneasy allies,

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: and every choice changes who gets to move—and who is left behind.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Fast routes fail. Worlds lose contact.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: People build lives across a slower, divided frontier.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: New passages reconnect distant communities—and reopen old rivalries.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Yes, it’s AI. Why? Because it was fun to put together. I wanted to imagine people with competing needs, put them on a frontier full of choices, and see what happened. Thanks for coming along.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY
dialogueInline.text: REX FLEET ACADEMY: REACH AND RESOLVE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A new generation enters the Fleet Academy to study history, doctrine, science, and navigation. But classroom rules meet real lives in the field.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Before the corridors reopened, generations grew up cut off. Follow the people who survived the collapse, formed new loyalties, and built futures in its long aftermath.

directionInline.text: This is a non-diegetic Issue 1 editorial close that introduces the series' promises and questions rather than advancing the issue's fictional events. Preserve every supplied text line exactly. Keep the editorial's focus on people living with survival, security, choice, separation, and home. The timeline must add world context without turning the page into a technical explanation. The AI note is candid, personal, and light. Do not reveal any story outcome beyond Issue 1.

source: Issue 1 end-matter editorial page approved by Jeff Hines, October 19, 2026.

title: Rex Fleet #2 — Previously
summary: Opening recap/title splash bridges released Issue 1 into Auric's next refugee crisis without altering the story pages.
settingText: AURIC APPROACH — THE GREEN CORRIDOR AND BAZAAR LIGHTS — NIGHT
panelPlan: Single full-page cinematic title/recap splash looking down a verified high-speed reciprocal-field corridor toward Auric's beautiful, inhabited rings and docking lights. Civilian traffic expands because the route dramatically shortens once-painfully-slow journeys.

The corridor is an engineered verified low-tension volume with beacon references, not a magical glowing tunnel or a debris-filled battle lane. Fleet and Shard silhouettes can frame distant politics without previewing the specific Issue 2 attack.
Reserve a broad dark field for the recap and issue-title typography. The art should feel like the calm after Issue 1 that is already beginning to fill with more traffic.
Do not depict any specific Issue 2 rescue action or outcome. The page may imply approaching pressure but must not reveal who survives the next crisis.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The reblazed Green Corridor made distant settlements close again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric needed heat. Refugees needed passage.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Halev negotiated Verge control. Fleet agreed to patrol.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Admiralty saw an exposed throat.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And the Shards were already arguing over whether the road belonged to anyone at all.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That only made more people try to use it.

directionInline.text: This is a non-diegetic opening title/recap page. Preserve every supplied caption exactly. Use released Rex Fleet Issue 1 as the strict visual baseline. The page should re-establish the corridor, Auric and the competing political claims without inventing new lore or previewing Issue 2's resolution.

title: From the Editor — After the Rescue
summary: Issue 2 end matter reflects on the issue's character-led conflict and frontier consequences, adds a brief world note, and points readers to Rex Fleet #3.

panelPlan: A genuine end-matter editorial page, distinct from the existing full-page next-issue teaser. Keep the approved STAR SPLITTER VISIONS / REX FLEET masthead treatment consistent with the other issue pages; identify this as ISSUE 2.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Mercy of Dawn reaches Auric, but a safe landing is only the beginning. Naomi has brought families through the fire; now Halev must find them shelter in a city already short on heat and medicine. Every open berth belongs to someone’s life, and every choice leaves a neighbor carrying the cost.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Venn risks her career to save the passengers, then refuses to turn rescue into authority over the people she saved. Richard and Paul keep fighting for their family and the strangers beside them. Tess helps across a battle line, while Abby and Billie face a rupture that friendship alone cannot mend. What does protection mean when the emergency is over?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric’s Crown Ring was built for comfort. Its empty apartments are not empty histories: doors, family belongings, failing heaters, and the people newly sheltered there all make competing claims on the same home.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric saved the ship. Now its survivors have to find a place in the city—and a way to live beside the people already there.

directionInline.text: This is a non-diegetic editorial end-matter page. Preserve every supplied line exactly and prioritize legibility over spectacle.

title: Next: Rex Fleet #3
summary: Closing teaser turns Auric's successful rescue into a domestic pressure-cooker: shelter exists, but ownership, heat and coexistence are unresolved.

panelPlan: Single full-page teaser splash centered on a grand but exhausted luxury-ring corridor converted into emergency shelter. Refugee bedding, old family possessions, utility heaters and sealed apartment doors should share the same space.
Use one doorway as the central visual argument: signs that a family once lived there remain visible while displaced people now sleep nearby. No one is posed as villain or intruder.
Do not reveal the deliberate-shortage records, Billie's later attack, or any Issue 3 resolution. Hint that the refuge itself is becoming contested.
Reserve clean negative space for the teaser text and let the final hook land against the closed doorway.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now it has to live with everyone who came off it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The luxury ring has empty rooms.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some of them still belong to people.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And everyone who survived the crossing needs something the city does not have enough of.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NOW THEY HAVE TO SURVIVE EACH OTHER.

directionInline.text: This is a non-diegetic closing teaser. Preserve the supplied wording exactly. dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Venn spent her command getting it through.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

dialogueInline.text: A HOME IS NOT A BERTH

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric’s crisis has no clean villain and no easy room to spare. A returning family wants its apartment back; refugees need warmth tonight. Halev has to govern people whose claims are real, while Naomi insists that a temporary berth cannot become a permanent answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Richard and Paul put names and testimony to the choices that left Tal Corvus families without heat or medicine. Abby risks her standing to protect civilians; Billie and Tess discover how far fear can carry a trusted friend. And as Venn faces judgment, the people she rescued are still living with the consequences. When does a rescue become a promise—and who gets to keep it?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The fast Green Corridor brings more than ships. It accelerates migration, trade, and pressure on housing, so Auric’s old shortage becomes a frontier-wide argument about who belongs.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The next evacuation window is open. Families are ready to run, but every escort has a different idea of what protection should cost.

title: Next: Rex Fleet #4

settingText: TAL CORVUS — PRE-DAWN EVACUATION ROUTE — VIOLET HAZE
panelPlan: Single full-page teaser splash. Families move in a thin line through jagged Tal Corvus terrain toward distant boarding lights under violet pre-dawn haze.

Far above or beyond the route, restrained Fleet and Shard silhouettes make clear that multiple armed parties can see the same corridor. Thunderbreak may appear only as a distant recognizable silhouette approaching, not yet intervening.
Keep the civilians visually dominant. Their exposed movement through a known route is the danger.
Leave the upper sky open for the teaser typography; the last two hook lines should land over the exposed route.

dialogueInline.text: Auric Gate is full of people before the battle begins. Venn keeps a lane open even when it weakens her formation. Naomi and Halev commit the Verge to keeping the crossing usable. Tess guides civilians through with Gravefire itself when the markers fail.

title: From the Editor — End of the First Run
summary: Final run-ending editorial page steps outside the fiction to reflect on how Rex Fleet grew during production and what kinds of stories the universe can hold next. Includes a restrained next-run notice: Rex Fleet returns soon.
settingText: STAR SPLITTER VISIONS EDITORIAL PAGE — DEEP-SPACE PRODUCTION STUDY / CORRIDOR MOTIFS
panelPlan: Design this as a genuine end-of-run editorial page rather than a story splash. Use one large quiet piece of Rex Fleet art—ships disappearing toward a luminous corridor—plus a restrained strip of small production-study motifs such as ship silhouettes, corridor-beacon geometry or location thumbnails.

Keep the artwork subordinate to the letter. Reserve a large, calm, high-contrast text column with magazine-quality spacing and hierarchy. This page should feel like Star Splitter Visions speaking directly to the reader after the story ends.
Do not create fake handwritten notes, fake creator signatures, fake logos, or invented credits. Do not recap Issue 12 visually or tease a specific unannounced Issue 13 plot.
The closing REX FLEET WILL RETURN line should have clear separation and final-page weight.
Add a restrained NEXT REX FLEET / COMING SOON line as a small lower-page callout. No Issue 13 title, cover, or plot details are in the current data; do not invent them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: When we started building Rex Fleet, the idea was much smaller than the universe it eventually demanded.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The starting point was the corridors: if civilization depends on a network of routes through dangerous space, somebody has to maintain them, defend them, map them and decide who gets to use them. From there came the Fleet, the Verge and the Shards—not simply as opposing factions, but as people with very different relationships to the same roads.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That gave us the world. The characters changed the book.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tess, Abby, Naomi, Venn, Jex, Billie and the rest gradually stopped feeling like pieces positioned around a political conflict and started pulling the story in their own directions. Some relationships became more important than we expected. Characters who seemed destined for one role refused to stay there. A story that began with fleets and borders increasingly became about what people do when the institution they belong to no longer gives them an adequate answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Rift changed too. Early on, it was primarily the environment through which these people traveled. By the time we reached the Calm Corridor and the Mirror Star, it had become something much stranger. We still know more about what the Rift can do than the characters do—but not nearly enough to make it comfortable.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Making these twelve issues also taught us what Rex Fleet itself wants to be. It can hold battleships and refugee skiffs, political arguments and engineering problems, strange physics, marketplaces, old grudges, bad jokes and people trying to get dinner through a checkpoint. The enormous things work better when the ordinary things remain visible underneath them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is the part we want to keep exploring.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This issue closes the first major Rex Fleet story, but it does not close the universe. There are ships we have barely visited, regions we have only named, histories that have only been hinted at, and parts of the Lattice that nobody in this book has seen.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Most importantly, there are still stories we want to tell with these people.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Thank you for reading all the way to the end of the first run—and for giving us the chance to find out what Rex Fleet could become.
